title: Stutter-Invariance Metamorphic Audits for Text World-Model Rollouts

contributions.purpose: Provide a principled way to audit the reliability of LLM text world-model rollouts.
contributions.mechanism: Formalize a stutter-invariance metamorphic relation: inserting state-preserving commands (e.g., look in TextWorld) should not affect subsequent predictions.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a formal metamorphic relation for text world models (no numeric metric for the formalization itself).
contributions.domain: Metamorphic testing of LLM text world models
contributions.source_quote: We formalize the stutter-invariance metamorphic relation for text world models, providing a principled approach to auditing rollout reliability.

contributions.purpose: Operationalize the metamorphic relation into a working audit.
contributions.mechanism: Implement a three-stage audit pipeline with embedding-based drift measurement and exponentially-weighted aggregation.
contributions.evaluation: Pipeline inserts look commands after each action and measures observation drift via embedding distance.
contributions.source_quote: We implement a three-stage audit pipeline with embedding-based drift measurement and exponentially-weighted aggregation.

contributions.purpose: Rigorously evaluate the audit against baselines.
contributions.mechanism: Compare against four baselines across three random seeds with pre-registered success criteria and bootstrap confidence intervals.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on TextWorld with a Qwen2.5-7B world model (W2R failure rate ~34%).
contributions.source_quote: We conduct rigorous evaluation with pre-registered success criteria, comparing against four baselines across three random seeds with bootstrap confidence intervals.

contributions.purpose: Report the empirical outcome of the audit for W2R failure prediction.
contributions.mechanism: Contrast the stutter-invariance audit AUROC against a simpler sampling-consistency baseline that re-runs generation with different seeds.
contributions.evaluation: Method achieves AUROC 0.767 but is statistically tied with the sampling-consistency baseline (AUROC 0.757), indicating no measurable advantage.
contributions.source_quote: We report an informative negative result: while our method achieves AUROC 0.767, it is statistically tied with a simpler sampling consistency baseline (AUROC 0.757), suggesting that domain-specific metamorphic probes do not provide measurable advantage over generic stability testing for this task.

self_declared_provenance.quote: MDPMorph (Li et al. 2025a) extends this approach to deep reinforcement learning agents, defining metamorphic relations over MDP transitions. Our stutter-invariance audit applies metamorphic testing principles to world model reliability, using domain-specific invariants (state-preserving commands) to detect unreliable rollouts.

Our work addresses a related but distinct problem: predicting whether a world model rollout will transfer successfully to the real environment, rather than optimizing policies under model uncertainty.
Unlike prior work that tests agent policies, we test the world model's ability to maintain consistent state representations.

notes: Explicit negative/tie result: authors frame it as an 'informative negative result' - the proposed stutter-invariance audit (AUROC 0.767) is statistically tied with a simpler sampling-consistency baseline (AUROC 0.757), so the domain-specific probe adds no measurable benefit.
